title: M2: Remote lab authority and publication-bound reference decisions
description:
PLANNING ONLY. Ryan requested filing and design before implementation. This issue is not authorization to build runtime features, deploy, change cloud permissions, publish packages, push, or migrate production data. Keep open pending design review and separate implementation authorization.

Future milestone: one remote cyclotron consumes common reference items, predicts independently for multiple publication outputs, and serves authorized Papyrus deployments. The remote lab alone owns canonical history, labels, learning and classifier state.

Future Definition of Done: two publications can disagree on the same item; authorized feedback affects only intended outputs; clients clearly show pending/unavailable states during outages; duplicate delivery/retries do not invent labels or duplicate learning. Authentication mechanism, tenancy boundary, binding schema and availability policy require design review.

Preserve optional curated-example priming (decision-flywheel-da886c09-7acb-45d3-acf8-c81585f26d8a), its preview/revision/explicit-label acceptance contract, and separate existing scholarly research-paper and web-summary transformations. Priming must never become an onboarding gate. Common input items are distinct from publication-specific decisions; one publication accepting an item must never implicitly label another output.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Ryan explicitly authorizes local implementation and testing of BOTH modes: "Oh okay, well we can start those. We are going to work on testing both ways." This supersedes the earlier planning-only implementation hold for local work. First vertical slice: shared publication contract over real Cyclotron facade, direct embedded and local HTTP remote-lab invocation, deterministic offline models, scoped labels/explanations/history/status, retry identity and restart. First specs failed because publication_lab did not exist; initial implementation now passes nine local tests. No paid calls, new cloud resources/permissions, production hosting or public push authorized. Persistence remains injected and owned by /task-4 storage conversion (45f8ee15057a069eb961b6a01e0240ca29fb1476; docs/storage-portability.md read). No competing adapter or persistent EC2 SQLite hosting. Local SQLite is only existing test-fixture storage; hosted activation remains unavailable pending full storage conversion/coordinator decisions. Papyrus UI integration remains coordinated via parent with /task-2 owner.
